column1: # Mission photographs: Fusion's photo events (#75). tools/pack.py packs each row with a situation into its reel: the
# image as a media member, media/<frame in lower case>.jpg from the reel's source folder, and the row as an entry of the
# reel's page.json `photos` and a photo entry of its event listing. A row without a situation stays here as research
# and is on no tape.
# frame: NASA frame number. reel: the scenario reel the photograph belongs to, <mission folder>-<scenario file stem>.
# get: seconds from that reel's range zero (Apollo 8 1968-12-21 12:51:00 UTC, Apollo 11 1969-07-16 13:32:00 UTC); blank if unknown.
# get_lo, get_hi: seconds, the bracket when only a range is known.
# get_src: source of the time and its precision; "unverified" marks our research not yet checked against a primary source.
# lens_mm: focal length. magazine: magazine number/letter. window_or_vehicle: where it was taken from, and by whom.
# sit: the situation that best fits, by its SITUATION card's ID in the reel (each reel numbers its own), blank if none.
# needs: what the sim lacks to reproduce the frame.
# url: the scan we reduced (apollojournals.org AFJ/ALSJ; reference/photos/ holds our 2048 px copies). credit: NASA/JSC, public domain.
# turn: quarter turns clockwise from the scan to the photograph's usual presentation, applied when tools/photo_pack.py
# reduces the scan to the packed copy (1024 px long side, JPEG quality 80), so the packed photograph is presented as is.
# cam_yaw, cam_pitch, cam_roll, fit_x, fit_y, fit_rot, fit_scale, fit_note: our fit (ours, made on the reduced scan
# against the kernel's Earth disc and lunar horizon), blank where there is none: the pointing added to the situation's
# default look (deg), the photograph's centre in plot degrees, its rotation (deg counterclockwise) and scale (% of the
# lens's field on the 55.74 mm gate), and what still misfits. Fusion's Copy alignment gives these numbers.
